name: PneumoScan AI - ResNet ensemble for pneumonia detection
authors: Umer Basith G (CSDX530 Deep Learning mini project, BSARCIST)
architecture: Ensemble of ImageNet-pretrained ResNets (torchvision), fine-tuned end-to-end with a 2-class head; horizontal-flip test-time augmentation; temperature-scaled probability; decision threshold chosen on validation. Grad-CAM from layer4 for explanations. See models/ensemble.json for the exact members.
input: One frontal chest X-ray image (JPG, PNG, 16-bit PNG or DICOM converted by the app). Converted to 8-bit grayscale, squashed to a square and resized to the network resolution.
output: Label NORMAL or PNEUMONIA, calibrated probability of pneumonia, risk level (Low / Moderate / High) and a Grad-CAM heatmap.
intended_use: Education and classroom demonstration of deep learning for medical imaging, and decision support for discussion only. The output is a second opinion that must be reviewed by a qualified clinician.
not_intended_for: Diagnosing, ruling out or treating pneumonia in real patients
Use as a medical device or replacement for a radiologist or doctor
Adults: the training data are paediatric chest X-rays (children aged 1-5 years)
Lateral views, CT scans, other body parts or other lung diseases (TB, COVID-19, cancer, effusion...)
training_data: Kermany et al. 2018, Chest X-Ray Images (Pneumonia), Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center, Mendeley Data DOI 10.17632/rscbjbr9sj.2, CC BY 4.0. Official train split (5,232 images) divided at patient level into train (4,485) and validation (747).
evaluation_data: Official held-out test split of the same dataset: 624 images (234 NORMAL, 390 PNEUMONIA). Used only for final reporting; nothing was tuned on it.
risk_levels: Low: probability below half the decision threshold. Moderate: between half the threshold and the midpoint between the threshold and 1 (borderline or possible pneumonia). High: above that midpoint. Exact cut-offs are in models/ensemble.json (risk_bands).
xray_gate: Images that are not chest X-rays (colour photos, documents, blank or tiny images, objects far from the training distribution) are rejected before prediction using colour/blank checks and a Mahalanobis distance on ResNet features. The gate is a convenience, not a guarantee: it can still accept other grayscale radiographs.
limitations: Single hospital, single paediatric population: performance on other hospitals, scanners or adults is unknown and usually lower (dataset shift, Zech et al. 2018).
Binary task only: it does not tell bacterial from viral pneumonia and does not detect other diseases.
Most errors on the official test set are NORMAL images predicted as PNEUMONIA (false alarms).
Grad-CAM heatmaps are coarse (from a 12x12 or 14x14 layer4 feature map) and show where the network looked, not where the disease is proven to be.
Labels come from expert graders but are not perfect; some training images are low quality.
Grad-CAM sometimes highlights burned-in text (the 'R' side marker, exposure values, time stamps) as well as the lungs, a sign of partial shortcut learning from hospital-specific image features.
Because the decision threshold (chosen on validation) is low, a PNEUMONIA label can come with a modest probability; the risk level is the better summary than the 'confidence' number.
ethical_considerations: Not a medical device. Never use the result alone to start, stop or withhold treatment. Patient data entered in the app stays on the local computer.
disclaimer: PneumoScan AI is an educational decision-support tool, not a medical device. It can be wrong. Always consult a qualified doctor.
